entries.translation_version: Mishnah Yomit by Dr. Joshua Kulp
entries.interpretive_summary: Records a minority position even when the majority governs, preserving a basis for later reconsideration.
entries.counter_reading: Preserving dissent does not mean every rejected view remains equally authoritative or should control present decisions.
analogy_guardrails: Do not equate a modern policy minority with a named rabbinic authority.
Separate preservation of dissent from adoption of dissent.

entries.interpretive_summary: Holds together recognition of competing views and the practical need to decide, while associating adjudicative preference with how opposing views are handled.
entries.counter_reading: Acknowledging plurality does not eliminate the need for a binding decision or establish that every position is equally applicable.
analogy_guardrails: Do not use the passage as generic proof that both AI-policy positions are true.
Name the decision rule separately from recognition of plurality.

entries.interpretive_summary: Contrasts extraordinary authority claims with an established human interpretive and decision procedure.
entries.counter_reading: The narrative concerns a particular legal-theological institution and cannot simply be converted into a general endorsement of majoritarian governance.
analogy_guardrails: Do not equate model outputs, scientific evidence, or expert testimony with a divine voice.
State which modern institution and decision rule are actually being compared.

entries.interpretive_summary: Treats careful hearing of opposed rulings as a disciplined intellectual task rather than a defect to erase prematurely.
entries.counter_reading: Hearing conflicting positions does not itself supply a rule for deciding between them.
analogy_guardrails: Use it to test listening and classification, not to declare contradictions resolved.
Identify what additional decision procedure the modern dispute requires.

entries.interpretive_summary: Makes the absence of any case for acquittal a procedural problem in a capital case, emphasizing the need for genuine adversarial consideration.
entries.counter_reading: A rule for capital adjudication is not a general claim that consensus is suspicious in every domain.
analogy_guardrails: Do not generalize from capital procedure to all consensus processes.
Specify the high-stakes feature that makes adversarial review relevant.

entries.interpretive_summary: Shows repeated suppression or humiliation of dissent becoming grounds for institutional accountability.
entries.counter_reading: The episode does not establish a complete theory of leadership removal or map directly onto modern governance structures.
analogy_guardrails: Compare patterns of accountability, not offices or personalities.
Distinguish disagreement from misuse of institutional power.

entries.translation_version: Mishnah Yomit by Dr. Joshua Kulp
entries.interpretive_summary: Joins patient judgment, broad learning, and protective boundaries as institutional practices.
entries.counter_reading: A protective boundary can also become excessive or detached from the risk it was meant to address.
analogy_guardrails: Do not translate a fence automatically into maximal AI restriction.
Name the protected value, failure mode, and cost of the safeguard.

entries.translation_version: Mishnah Yomit by Dr. Joshua Kulp
entries.interpretive_summary: Frames responsibility as real even when no individual can complete the whole task.
entries.counter_reading: An open-ended obligation does not determine which actor should do what or justify ineffective action.
analogy_guardrails: Use it to examine allocation of responsibility, not to excuse the absence of measurable outcomes.
Require a named actor and feasible next action.

entries.interpretive_summary: Uses reciprocity as a compact ethical orientation while treating the remaining work as requiring further study and application.
entries.counter_reading: Reciprocity alone may not resolve collective-risk, distributional, or non-symmetric policy problems.
analogy_guardrails: Do not reduce all AI governance to individual interpersonal reciprocity.
Test whether affected parties and power relationships are actually symmetric.

entries.interpretive_summary: Treats uncertainty involving danger more stringently than uncertainty involving ordinary prohibition.
entries.counter_reading: The principle does not specify probability thresholds, define which AI hazards count as danger, or erase proportionality concerns.
analogy_guardrails: Require an explicit account of the alleged danger and uncertainty.
Do not invoke precaution without discussing probability, magnitude, and intervention cost.

entries.interpretive_summary: Contrasts satisfying the legal minimum with conduct beyond that minimum and connects rigid legalism to social failure.
entries.counter_reading: Going beyond formal duty can be indeterminate, unevenly imposed, or unsuitable as a substitute for enforceable rules.
analogy_guardrails: Distinguish voluntary responsibility from enforceable regulation.
Ask who bears the extra burden and how compliance is assessed.

entries.interpretive_summary: Uses a shifting relationship between private property and shared space to expose the shortsighted externalization of hazards.
entries.counter_reading: The story does not by itself determine how diffuse digital harms should be attributed or regulated.
analogy_guardrails: Name the modern public domain, the transferred hazard, and the responsible actor.
Do not assume every downstream risk is traceable to one owner or developer.
